concept.name: Flickering quote
concept.definition: A quotation that appears and disappears on extremely short timescales, produced by millisecond-lived limit orders that are cancelled almost immediately. Hasbrouck and Saar document such fleeting order and quoting behavior as a hallmark of low-latency trading, and Regulation NMS Rule 611(b)(8) accommodates it via the one-second flickering-quote exception to trade-through liability.
concept.intuition: These are quotes that blink in and out faster than slower participants can react to them.
concept.mechanics: High-frequency market makers continuously update and cancel quotes to manage inventory and avoid adverse selection, so a large share of displayed liquidity lives for only milliseconds; consolidated feeds may never fully capture the fastest flickers.
concept.failure_modes: Quote-based liquidity metrics overstate accessible liquidity when much of it flickers, and flickering undermines the reliability of quote-midpoint benchmarks used for best-execution and trade-classification analysis.
concept.misconceptions: Flickering quotes are not necessarily phantom or spoofed orders; most are bona fide but very short-lived quotes reflecting legitimate high-frequency risk management.
concept.example: A 100-share offer at the NBO exists for 3 milliseconds before being cancelled and reposted one tick away, repeating hundreds of times per second.

citations.source: Hasbrouck and Saar, 'Low-Latency Trading', Journal of Financial Markets 16(4):646-679 (author-hosted copy)
citations.section: Full text (fleeting orders and flickering quotes)
